Confirm step 3.3 is in: rg -n 'lastWorkedAt' src/db/schema.ts finds it in cronJobs and rg -n 'export function workedOf' src/server/cron-runs.ts finds the function; if either is missing, stop. refreshEmbeddings() (rg -n 'export async function refreshEmbeddings' src/server/embeddings.ts) takes `options: { now?: Date; full?: boolean } = {}` (step 0.28 added it; if step 3.3 removed it with the minute guard, add it back with exactly that type). At its top, before `aiFor(null, ...)`, write `const now = options.now ?? new Date(); const full = options.full ?? now.getUTCHours() === 3;` and, when full is false, send one statement read with `typedRow(z.object({ changed: col.bool }), sql\`...\`)` (import z from 'zod' and typedRow and col from './typed-rows' where the file lacks them): `select exists (select 1 from commerce.product_translations t where t.text_changed_at > coalesce(j.last_started_at, '-infinity'::timestamptz)) or coalesce(j.last_worked_at >= j.last_started_at, false) or coalesce(j.last_error_at >= j.last_started_at, false) as changed from (select 1) as one left join commerce.cron_jobs j on j.job = 'dispatcher.embeddings'`. When changed is not true, return { embedded: 0, failed: 0 } and send nothing else (no aiFor, no ai_providers read, no staleTranslations). Why each clause holds (put this in the function's doc comment, shortened): the ledger row is written when a run finishes (record() in src/server/cron-runs.ts), so while this run reads it, it holds the previous run. (1) last_started_at is when that run began, so a text changed while it ran is newer and is not missed; with no row yet, '-infinity' makes any translation count. (2) step 3.3 sets last_worked_at to the finish time only when workedOf() found embedded or failed above 0, so last_worked_at >= last_started_at means the previous run embedded something (it may have left more than PER_RUN, 256 per AI) or failed at the provider (embedWith() returns failed instead of throwing): the sweep reads on until one run embeds nothing and fails nothing, and stops after that run. (3) last_error_at >= last_started_at means the previous run threw (a statement timeout, a database error): record() still wrote its last_started_at, so without this clause a text changed before that run would wait for the 03 UTC net. A new translation gets now() from the column's default, so it counts as changed. Also write in the doc comment what the probe does not see and the full run at UTC hour 3 catches (at most a day late, then 256 per AI an hour through clause 2): a category or tag added to, removed from or renamed on a product (commerce.product_terms and commerce.terms, the third input of the hash in staleTranslations()); a product's status changed by a path that does not call refreshStoreEmbeddings() (the savers in the file's top comment do); a store that becomes active; a changed embedding model or provider (commerce.ai_providers has no timestamp: meaning search finds nothing for those stores until the net re-embeds them, keyword search goes on); and a save whose transaction began before a run started and committed after its probe (text_changed_at is the transaction's now()). Also replace `commerce.store_is_active(t.store_id)` in staleTranslations() by `join commerce.stores s on s.id = t.store_id` (after the join to commerce.products) and, in the where, `s.status = 'active' and not s.starter and not s.sandbox`: the function's whole body is `SELECT COALESCE((SELECT s.status = 'active' AND NOT s.starter AND NOT s.sandbox FROM commerce.stores s WHERE s.id = p_store), false)` (baseline_1_schema.sql line 18852), and a join gives the same rows because a translation's store always exists.
